newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Horse Racing-Imperial call favourite for Hennessy.
newsitem.headline: Horse Racing-Imperial call favourite for Hennessy.

text.p: Ireland's Cheltenham Gold Cup hero, Imperial Call, on Friday headed a star-studded field for Sunday's Grade One Hennessy Gold Cup at Leopardstown.
Imperial Call (evens favourite) faces seven rivals, three trained in Britain, including 1993 Cheltenham Gold Cup winner, Jodami, in Sunday's three mile (4.8-km) contest.
Fergie Sutherland-trained Imperial Call, a faller on his seasonal bow at Punchestown, came to prominence with a victory in the 100,000 ($159,900) presentataion last year.
"He's in super form, but I would love to see a drop of rain," Sutherland said.
The official Leopardstown going on Friday was good, but the forecast is for showers at the weekend which would favour Imperial Call.

Peter Beaumont-trained Jodami, winner of three successive Hennessy Gold Cups starting in 1993, was denied the chance to bid for a four-timer by an 11th hour setback 12 months ago. He has eased out from 7-2 to 11-2.
Gordon Richards-trained The Grey Monk heads the British challenge at 7-2 while Paul Nicholls-trained Belmont King, winner of the Rehearsal Chase, is quoted at 10-1.
Britain has won the race eight times in its 10-year history.
Ireland's latest equine star, Danoli, a faller on two of his five starts over fences this season and Jim Dreaper-trained Merry Gale are both quoted at 8-1.
Arthur Moore-trained King of the Gales and Aidan O'Brien's Idiots Venture, both at 33-1, complete the field.
County Limerick-based handler Michael Hourigan has elected to run Dorans Pride in the Grade Two Scalp Chase, over two miles and five furlongs (4.0-km), rather than Sunday's Gold Cup.
"I had a word with Tom Doran (owner) and with so many good horses likely to run in the Hennessy we have decided to keep our fellow in the novice ranks," Hourigan said early in the week.
"Dorans Pride is well and we will just hope for another win in the Scalp Chase before making up our minds about his Cheltenham target," he added.

Dorans Pride will renew rivalry with Paul Nicholls-trained See More Business at Leopardstown. A length separated the pair when they met at Fairyhouse on December 1, with Hourigan's stable-star emerging the winner on that occasion.
Aidan O'Brien-trained Istabraq will use the Deloitte and Touche Novice Hurdle over two miles and two furlongs (3.6-km) as a warm-up race for one of the top novice hurdle races at Cheltenham in March.
